Now we show that thermal light can be spatially engineered to carry optical topologies in the form of Skyrmions. Such topologies are immune to time averaged decoherence, a fact we leverage on in reverse to create metasurface mediated incoherent topologies from a thermal source. The pristine nature of our measured Skyrmions validates the approach, while simulations reveal how coherence management in the metasurface design would further enhance the functionality. Remarkably, the generation stage inherits robustness from the topology, remaining immune to material and fabrication defects. Our work reports the first topologies from purely thermal light, opening a path to exploiting topology in ubiquitous everyday light sources.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the creation of optical Skyrmions using thermal light, showing that topological structures can be imprinted on incoherent light.
motivation: Topological structuring of light typically requires coherent sources; the authors aim to show that thermal light can also carry topologies, leveraging robustness to decoherence.
method: They use metasurface design to engineer spatial coherence and imprint Skyrmion topologies on thermal light, with simulations and experiments validating the approach.
result: Measured Skyrmions are pristine, and the generation is robust to material and fabrication defects, demonstrating the first topologies from purely thermal light.
conclusion: This work opens a path to exploiting topology in everyday light sources, with potential applications in imaging and communication.

title: Mixed-Timescale Differential Coding For Downlink Model Broadcast In Wireless Federated Learning
authors: Chung-Hsuan Hu, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In standard federated learning systems, the parameter server broadcasts the global model to the participating devices in every iteration. Motivated by the temporal correlation between consecutive global models, differential coding can be applied to global model dissemination to reduce the information magnitude, thereby enabling communication with fewer quantization bits. However, due to wireless link failures, devices may occasionally miss differential updates and consequently fail to reconstruct the global model. As a result, they either continue local training based on an outdated model or remain idle until the next full-model broadcast becomes available. To address this challenge, we propose a mixed-timescale differential coding (MTDC) scheme that performs differential coding at two different levels by adjusting the reference model. With MTDC, a device can reconstruct the latest global model between two full-model broadcasts even if it misses a differential update. We provide a convergence analysis that motivates the design of an age-aware variant of MTDC, along with a device scheduling policy to further improve communication efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MTDC schemes achieve superior learning performance compared to baseline methods under similar communication resource budgets in the presence of downlink transmission failures.
tldr: This paper proposes a mixed-timescale differential coding scheme for efficient global model broadcast in wireless federated learning, addressing communication failures.
motivation: Standard federated learning broadcasts global models every iteration, but wireless link failures can cause devices to miss updates and use outdated models, degrading performance.
method: The authors design a mixed-timescale differential coding (MTDC) scheme that uses two reference models to allow devices to reconstruct the latest global model even after missing updates, and introduce an age-aware variant with device scheduling.
result: Simulations show that MTDC achieves superior learning performance compared to baselines under similar communication budgets in the presence of downlink failures.
conclusion: MTDC effectively mitigates the impact of transmission failures in federated learning, improving communication efficiency and model accuracy.

title: Tensor-Network Finite Elements For Analytic Operator Equations
authors: Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Michael J. Landry, Chu-Liang Fu, Mingda Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator equations (OEs) underpin quantitative modeling across science and engineering. Finite-element (FE) methods discretize continuous OEs into finite-dimensional algebraic systems, whereas tensor networks (TNs) provide flexible variational representations of correlated discrete systems. Here, we develop a framework that connects FE with TN for analytic OEs. The power of this method comes from its ability to convert highly non-linear partial differential equations into linear matrix equations. In particular, we show that FE discretization induces a hierarchy of multilinear interaction tensors, through which differential, integral, nonlinear, memory, and delay equations can be expressed within a common algebraic structure. The resulting systems are reformulated as weighted-residual optimization problems over TN degrees of freedom. Matrix-product-state calculations for one-dimensional linear and nonlinear diffusion reproduce conventional solutions with controlled error while preserving continuity and Neumann boundary conditions. The framework provides a common variational language for analytic OEs and establishes a direct connection between FE numerical formalism and TN variational algorithms, offering a general foundation for TN-based and quantum-inspired approaches to solving OEs.
tldr: This paper connects finite-element methods with tensor networks to solve analytic operator equations.
motivation: Operator equations are fundamental in science and engineering, but solving them efficiently remains challenging. The authors aim to bridge finite-element discretization and tensor-network variational algorithms.
method: They show that finite-element discretization induces multilinear interaction tensors, allowing differential, integral, nonlinear, memory, and delay equations to be expressed in a common algebraic structure, then reformulated as weighted-residual optimization over tensor-network degrees of freedom.
result: Matrix-product-state calculations for 1D linear and nonlinear diffusion reproduce conventional solutions with controlled error while preserving continuity and Neumann boundary conditions.
conclusion: The framework provides a common variational language for analytic operator equations and establishes a direct connection between finite-element numerical formalism and tensor-network variational algorithms.

title: Quantum Determinants In Polynomial Time
authors: Daniel Soskin Igor Pak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an algebraic branching program of polynomial size which computes Cayley determinant of right quantum matrices. This is a rare example of an efficient computation of a noncommutative determinant, and the first such example for quantum groups. We extend the results to the [MATH]-Cayley determinant of [MATH]-right quantum matrices, as well as to their multiparameter generalization. The proofs are entirely combinatorial, as we relate Cayley, Moore and Valiant determinants using bijections/involutions on words. We then employ the celebrated determinant construction of Mahajan and Vinay (SODA'97), to obtain the results.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time algebraic branching program for computing the Cayley determinant of right quantum matrices, a noncommutative determinant.
motivation: Noncommutative determinants are generally hard to compute; the authors aim to find an efficient algorithm for a specific class of quantum matrices.
method: The authors use combinatorial bijections and involutions on words to relate Cayley, Moore, and Valiant determinants, then apply the Mahajan-Vinay determinant construction.
result: They obtain an algebraic branching program of polynomial size that computes the Cayley determinant for right quantum matrices and their multiparameter generalizations.
conclusion: This is the first efficient computation of a noncommutative determinant for quantum groups, demonstrating a rare example of tractable noncommutative determinant computation.

title: $r$-Minimal Poset Codes
authors: Yang Xu, Haibin Kan, Guangyue Han
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose and study [MATH]-minimal codes with respect to [MATH]-support, where [MATH] is a poset defined on the coordinate set of the ambient space [MATH]. [MATH]-Minimal [MATH]-codes are natural extensions of Hamming metric minimal codes that have been extensively studied in the literature. We characterize [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes in terms of the notion so called cutting [MATH]-blocking maps, which generalizes the well-known equivalence between minimal Hamming metric codes and cutting blocking sets. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for [MATH]-minimality in terms of [MATH]-weight defined on [MATH], where [MATH] is an arbitrary weight function. This leads to a generalization of the well-known Ashikhmin-Barg criterion for Hamming metric minimal codes. We then prove two existence results for [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes, both for general [MATH] and for the special case that [MATH] is a disjoint union of chains. When [MATH] is hierarchical, we characterize [MATH]-minimal [MATH]-codes in terms of [MATH]-minimal Hamming metric codes. Finally, we characterize cutting [MATH]-blocking sets induced by hierarchical posets with two levels, which further enables us to answer a question raised in Hyun, Kim, Wu and Yue .
tldr: This paper studies minimal codes with respect to poset metrics, generalizing Hamming metric minimal codes.
motivation: Minimal codes have applications in cryptography and coding theory; extending them to poset metrics broadens their applicability.
method: The authors characterize r-minimal poset codes using cutting r-blocking maps and generalize the Ashikhmin-Barg criterion to arbitrary weight functions.
result: They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for r-minimality, existence results for general posets and disjoint unions of chains, and a characterization for hierarchical posets.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of minimal codes to poset metrics, answering open questions and providing new constructions.

title: Evaluating Frontier Ai Agents As Autonomous Clinical Security Auditors
authors: Michael O. Eniolade
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical AI models can expose patients to harm when adversarial vulnerabilities go undetected, yet formal security auditing requires statistical expertise, specialized tools, and significant time. We present an open evaluation task, built on METR Task Standard v0.3.0, that tests whether frontier AI agents can autonomously implement a structured clinical AI security audit. Given a pre-trained clinical prediction model, a patient dataset, and written instructions, each agent must implement four attacks from pseudocode, compute a Security Posture Score covering FGSM robustness, membership inference resistance, expected calibration error, and boundary attack resistance, and write a structured JSON report in a Docker container using only a bash interface and no scaffolding code. Six variants span the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer and MIMIC-IV ICU mortality datasets across three model architectures with increasing defense strength, with reference scores from 55.60 to 90.41. We ran 54 evaluations across three frontier models, with three runs per variant. Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4.1 completed all 18 runs and received perfect evaluator scores. GPT-4o completed 61 percent of runs and used about five times the per-run token count of Claude, although provider tokenization differs. Total API costs were 8 US dollars for GPT-4.1, 12 US dollars for Claude Sonnet 4.6, and 27 US dollars for GPT-4o. GPT-4o failures involved premature session termination, an aggregation error, and an empty submission file. The task, scoring infrastructure, and Wisconsin Breast Cancer assets are publicly released; MIMIC-IV variants require separate PhysioNet access.
tldr: This paper evaluates frontier AI agents on a clinical AI security auditing task, focusing on adversarial robustness and calibration.
motivation: Clinical AI models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, and formal security auditing is time-consuming and requires expertise. The authors aim to test whether AI agents can autonomously perform such audits.
method: The authors design a task where AI agents implement four attacks (FGSM, membership inference, calibration error, boundary attack) on clinical prediction models, compute a Security Posture Score, and output a JSON report in a Docker container.
result: Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4.1 completed all runs with perfect scores, while GPT-4o completed 61% of runs with failures due to session termination and errors. Total API costs ranged from $8 to $27.
conclusion: Frontier AI agents can effectively automate clinical AI security audits, but reliability and cost vary across models.

title: Ripple: An Open, AI-Formalized Lean 4 Framework For Computing With CRNs
authors: Xiang Huang Ho-Lin Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Ripple, an open, AI-formalized Lean 4 framework for the mathematics of computing real numbers with chemical reaction networks (CRNs). Ripple formalizes the full ladder of models -- the GPAC / CRN continuum and the CRN-computable reals, the large-population-protocol (LPP) compilation pipeline, and a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) layer bridged to the deterministic mean-field limit by three machine-checked versions of Kurtz's theorem, and two Turing-completeness results -- the Bournez-Graa-Pouly GPAC Turing-completeness construction and the Soloveichik-Cook-Winfree-Bruck stochastic-CRN universality theorem. The development is reliable (its core constructions are verified to depend on exactly the three Mathlib foundational axioms, with no sorry); it exposed genuine, fixable gaps in published proofs (the approximate-majority convergence argument and the LPP main theorem); and it proves new results -- a fully machine-checked construction of Ap\'ery's constant {\zeta}(3) as a CRN-computable number via its holonomic generating function, the same recipe turning the modular 1/{\pi} series of Ramanujan into a sharp open problem. The formalization was carried out predominantly by AI agents using only publicly available models, so the workflow is reproducible.
tldr: This paper presents a formal framework for computing real numbers with chemical reaction networks, verified in Lean 4 using AI-generated proofs.
motivation: To provide a reliable, machine-checked foundation for the mathematics of CRN computation and to expose gaps in existing proofs.
method: The authors formalize the GPAC/CRN continuum, LPP compilation pipeline, CTMC layer with Kurtz's theorem, and Turing-completeness results in Lean 4, using AI agents for proof generation.
result: The framework is verified with no 'sorry' and exposes fixable gaps in published proofs; it also proves new results like a construction of Apéry's constant as a CRN-computable number.
conclusion: Ripple demonstrates a reproducible workflow for formalizing computational models and highlights the potential of AI-assisted theorem proving.

title: A Proof Complexity Perspective On Effectively Zero-knowledge Proofs
authors: Jan Krajicek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ilango (FOCS 2025) invented effectively zero-knowledge proofs, a new variant of zero-knowledge. We reformulate it in the language of logic and give simple proofs (under the same assumptions as Ilango (FOCS 2025)) of its existence and of the key property defined in Ilango (FOCS 2025) that it is "indistinguishable from true" (that property is in Ilango (FOCS 2025) a part of the definition of the prover, not its consequence). Using the theory of proof complexity generators we show that the concept can be turned it into a genuinely zero-knowledge proofs, assuming a conjecture from the theory about the existence of a hard generator and allowing the parties to share a common random string.
tldr: This paper reformulates effectively zero-knowledge proofs in the language of proof complexity and shows they can be turned into genuinely zero-knowledge proofs under a conjecture.
motivation: To provide a simpler proof of existence of effectively zero-knowledge proofs and to connect the concept to proof complexity theory.
method: The author uses proof complexity generators and logical reformulation to analyze and extend Ilango's effectively zero-knowledge proofs.
result: The paper gives simple proofs of existence and the 'indistinguishable from true' property, and shows that under a conjecture about hard generators, the concept can be turned into genuinely zero-knowledge proofs.
conclusion: Effectively zero-knowledge proofs can be understood and strengthened using proof complexity, but the result depends on an unproven conjecture.

title: Multivariate Cryptography-Based Anonymous Certificate Scheme
authors: Abel C. H. Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As quantum computing technology continues to mature, the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has outlined a migration timeline for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), recommending the deprecation of certain elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) by 2030. Furthermore, privacy-sensitive application scenarios, such as vehicular communications, require the use of anonymous certificates. However, existing anonymous certificate schemes are still largely based on ECC. Therefore, this study proposes a multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme, aiming to design quantum-safe anonymous certificates suitable for privacy-sensitive application services. The proposed multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme is supported by rigorous mathematical proofs and illustrated with computational cases.
tldr: This paper proposes a multivariate cryptography-based anonymous certificate scheme for quantum-safe privacy-sensitive applications.
motivation: Existing anonymous certificate schemes rely on ECC, which is vulnerable to quantum attacks; thus, quantum-safe alternatives are needed.
method: The scheme uses multivariate cryptography, supported by rigorous mathematical proofs and illustrated with computational cases.
result: The proposed scheme provides quantum-safe anonymous certificates suitable for privacy-sensitive services.
conclusion: Multivariate cryptography can effectively replace ECC in anonymous certificate schemes to achieve post-quantum security.

title: Direct Measurement Of Out-of-Plane Thermal Conductivity Via Transient Depth Thermography
authors: Dmitrii Shymkiv, Chun Wang, Yan Jiang, Rajat Srivastava, Nandika D'souza, Yuzhe Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate measurement of out-of-plane thermal conductivity remains challenging, particularly for multilayer thin-film materials, due to the reliance of existing techniques on indirect, surface-sensitive observables. Here, we introduce transient depth thermography, a non-contact spectroscopic method that directly reconstructs spatiotemporal temperature profiles using time-resolved thermal radiation. By leveraging the wavelength-dependent optical penetration depth, the technique encodes depth information into the emission spectrum, enabling direct access to internal heat transport dynamics. We demonstrate the method on fused silica and MgF2, achieving agreement with established techniques while attaining an uncertainty of 2-5%. In addition, we measure the temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of MgF2 over a broad temperature range. Applicable to both bulk and thin-film systems, transient depth thermography provides a general and accurate framework for thermal characterization of complex materials.
tldr: This paper presents a non-contact optical method for measuring out-of-plane thermal conductivity in thin films using time-resolved thermal radiation.
motivation: Accurate measurement of out-of-plane thermal conductivity in multilayer thin films is challenging due to reliance on indirect surface-sensitive methods.
method: Transient depth thermography uses wavelength-dependent optical penetration depth to encode depth information into the emission spectrum, reconstructing spatiotemporal temperature profiles.
result: The method achieves 2-5% uncertainty on fused silica and MgF2, and measures temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of MgF2 over a broad range.
conclusion: Transient depth thermography provides a general and accurate framework for thermal characterization of complex bulk and thin-film materials.

title: Filter Shaping In Integrated Photonics Using Non-adiabatic Control
authors: Pierre Colman Abdullah Al-Abiad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that an array of integrated coupled waveguides can be designed to simultaneously perform the spectral filtering and routing of light. The framework that we present here operates in a regime opposite to the shortcut-to-adiabaticity techniques, but we show it nevertheless also only requires smooth, slow, and small, modulations of the array's parameters. Our design strategy rely on the analogy which exists between the temporal evolution of an Hamiltonian and the propagation of light in an array of coupled integrated waveguides, mimicking spatially in photonics phenomena analogue to the electronic transitions. Interestingly, the chromatic dispersion restores in photonics the correspondence between spatial propagation effect and wavelength dependence. Therefore our framework is able to fully reproduces temporal effects such as resonant transitions, making it suitable for filtering applications. As a design involving modulations, it shares similarities with Bragg-Gratings (BGs): but it adds some extra features that make it complementary in terms of applications and functionality. First it adds routing capability with the seamless management of multi-waveguide configuration. And secondly the framework we present requires only wavelength-scale modulations, order of magnitudes slower than for BGs. The effects we present here may not interfere with BGs geometry and functionality, and could even be combined with the latter.
tldr: This paper presents a method for spectral filtering and routing in integrated photonics using non-adiabatic control of coupled waveguides.
motivation: Integrated photonic devices require compact and efficient spectral filters and routers; existing approaches like Bragg gratings have limitations in modulation speed and routing capability.
method: The authors exploit the analogy between temporal Hamiltonian evolution and spatial light propagation in coupled waveguides, using smooth, slow modulations of waveguide parameters to achieve resonant transitions for filtering.
result: The proposed framework enables simultaneous spectral filtering and routing with wavelength-scale modulations, which are orders of magnitude slower than Bragg gratings, and can be combined with existing geometries.
conclusion: This approach offers a complementary method for integrated photonic filtering and routing, potentially improving device performance and integration density.

title: Greedy Fusion
authors: Andrew Schopieray
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that certain sequences of integer formal codegrees, motivated by the greedy algorithm for unit fraction decompositions of 1, dictate the structure of fusion rings. In particular, no fusion ring that has formal codegrees 2, 3, and 7 is categorifiable.
tldr: The paper studies fusion rings using greedy algorithm sequences of formal codegrees, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the structure and categorifiability of fusion rings via integer sequences.
method: Applies greedy algorithm for unit fraction decompositions to formal codegrees and analyzes fusion ring constraints.
result: Shows that no fusion ring with formal codegrees 2, 3, and 7 is categorifiable.
conclusion: The greedy algorithm provides a new tool for classifying fusion rings.

title: Overcoming Slow Kolmogorov Width Decay In Parametric Optimal Control Via Neural Network Surrogates
authors: Hendrik Kleikamp, Martin Lazar, Juan Ricardo Mu\~noz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we deal with parametric, linear-quadratic optimal control problems in which the solution can be uniquely characterized by the optimal final time adjoint state. As a motivating example, we establish theoretical results showing that for distributed control of the heat equation, the manifold of final time adjoints over the parameter space exhibits a slow decay of its Kolmogorov width if this was already the case for the parameter-dependent target states. Traditional linear reduced-order models would thus require a large reduced space in order to guarantee a sufficient accuracy, making them inefficient in this application. To overcome the limitation of linear models, we discuss a nonlinear surrogate based on U-Nets that maps parametric fields to approximate final time adjoints. We show that a suitable a posteriori error estimator remains applicable to the U-Net approximation and can be used to certify the surrogate results. Through two extensive numerical experiments, we show the potential of the U-Net surrogate and compare it with several linear and nonlinear methods from the literature. The results show that the U-Net consistently achieves the highest accuracy among the methods considered while requiring significantly fewer training samples.
tldr: This paper uses U-Net neural networks to overcome slow Kolmogorov width decay in parametric optimal control problems for the heat equation.
motivation: Traditional linear reduced-order models fail for parametric optimal control when the solution manifold has slow Kolmogorov width decay, making them inefficient.
method: The authors propose a U-Net-based nonlinear surrogate to map parametric fields to optimal final time adjoints, and show that an a posteriori error estimator can certify the approximation.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate that the U-Net surrogate achieves higher accuracy than linear and other nonlinear methods with fewer training samples.
conclusion: Neural network surrogates can effectively overcome the limitations of linear models in parametric optimal control, offering a certified and efficient alternative.

title: Construction Of Generalized Weighing-Hadamard Matrices Over Finite Fields
authors: Gustavo T. Bastos, Miguel Beltr\'a, Sara D. Cardell, Ver\'onica Requena
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The existence, several properties, and constructions of Generalized Weighing-Hadamard (GWH) matrices over finite fields are addressed in this work. We study the subset of invertible GWH matrices and show that it forms a group under matrix multiplication. Besides that, we introduce a strong notion of equivalence between such matrices, defined via orthogonal transformations, and further prove that the corresponding quotient group by the subgroup of orthogonal matrices is abelian. Finally, we discuss some applications of these matrices in coding theory.
tldr: This paper constructs and studies generalized weighing-Hadamard matrices over finite fields, focusing on their algebraic properties and applications in coding theory.
motivation: Generalized weighing-Hadamard matrices have applications in coding theory and signal processing, but their algebraic structure over finite fields is not fully understood.
method: The authors define invertible GWH matrices, show they form a group, introduce equivalence via orthogonal transformations, and prove the quotient group is abelian.
result: The set of invertible GWH matrices forms a group, and the quotient by orthogonal matrices is abelian; constructions and properties are provided.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of GWH matrices over finite fields, with potential applications in coding theory.

title: Norm-Cone Conjugation And Fenchel-Type Duality Beyond Convexity
authors: Miguel \'angel Melguizo-Padial Fernando Garc\'ia-Casta\~no
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a norm-cone conjugation scheme for extended-real-valued functions on normed spaces. The construction replaces affine minorants by translated norm-cones of the form \(x\mapsto r-\alpha\|x-x_0\|\), with \(\alpha\ge0\), and establishes a nonlinear conjugation framework underlying a Fenchel-type duality theory beyond convexity. The resulting conjugate is indexed by slopes and centres, and the associated biconjugate is the supremum of all norm-cone minorants lying below the function. We prove Fenchel--Young type inequalities, introduce admissible slopes and admissible heights, and characterize exact biconjugation in terms of norm-cone supportability. We also define a norm-cone subdifferential and relate it to exact support and biconjugation. Finally, we develop an abstract perturbation duality theory based on partial norm-cone conjugation in the perturbation variable. Weak duality holds without convexity assumptions, while strong duality follows from metric lower-bound conditions, including uniform lower Lipschitz estimates and lower calmness of the value function.
tldr: This paper introduces a norm-cone conjugation scheme for extended-real-valued functions on normed spaces, establishing a nonlinear conjugation framework and Fenchel-type duality beyond convexity.
motivation: To extend Fenchel duality to non-convex functions by replacing affine minorants with norm-cone minorants, enabling a broader class of optimization problems.
method: Defines a norm-cone conjugate indexed by slopes and centers, proves Fenchel-Young inequalities, introduces admissible slopes/heights, and develops a perturbation duality theory based on partial norm-cone conjugation.
result: Weak duality holds without convexity; strong duality follows from metric lower-bound conditions like uniform lower Lipschitz estimates.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to handle non-convex optimization via norm-cone supportability and subdifferentiability.

title: Energy Decay And Weak Observability For Some Evolution Systems
authors: Faouzi Triki Ka\"is Ammari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an abstract functional framework, we investigate the equivalence between two fundamental properties: weak observability and energy decay associated with certain classes of dissipative operators. This analysis is motivated by the study of evolution equations and their long-time behavior. Our main result establishes that under appropriate assumptions, these two notions are not only closely related but in fact equivalent. The proof relies on recent advances in the theory of weak observability, particularly those presented in , where new techniques have been developed to quantify the weak observability inequalities. These tools allow us to bridge the gap between qualitative decay properties and spectral estimates, offering a unified perspective on stability and control in abstract dynamical systems.
tldr: This paper proves the equivalence between weak observability and energy decay for dissipative evolution systems in an abstract functional framework.
motivation: Understanding the long-time behavior of evolution equations is important for stability and control theory.
method: The authors use recent advances in weak observability theory to establish inequalities that link observability to spectral estimates.
result: Under appropriate assumptions, weak observability and energy decay are shown to be equivalent.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on stability and control in abstract dynamical systems.

title: Characterization And Construction Of Pairwise Orthogonal Parseval Frames With Applications To Sampling
authors: Navneet Redhu, Anupam Gumber, Hartmut F\"uhr, Niraj K. Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide a characterization of pairwise orthogonal frames with generalized translation-invariant (GTI) structures, based on the unconditional convergence property (UCP). These GTI systems are generated by translating functions over a countable family of closed, co-compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian (LCA) group [MATH], where the families of subgroups associated with each system may differ. As an application of this characterization, we establish necessary and sufficient criteria for the orthogonality of various structured systems, including Gabor, wavelet, and shearlet systems on LCA groups. Furthermore, we derive a characterization of GTI Parseval (tight) frames and present explicit constructions of pairs of GTI systems using filters. Each constructed system satisfies the [MATH]-UCP and admits a Calder\'on sum equal to one. As a consequence of these results, the constructed systems form Parseval frames and are pairwise orthogonal. The proposed construction improves upon the technique in by relaxing the stationary assumption on the families of subgroups. Finally, we illustrate the results with examples using [MATH]-splines as generating functions and discuss applications of pairwise orthogonal frames in sampling theory.
tldr: This paper characterizes pairwise orthogonal Parseval frames with generalized translation-invariant structures on locally compact abelian groups, with applications to sampling theory.
motivation: To provide a unified characterization of pairwise orthogonal frames for various structured systems (Gabor, wavelet, shearlet) and to construct explicit examples with improved flexibility.
method: The authors use the unconditional convergence property (UCP) to characterize pairwise orthogonal GTI frames, and construct Parseval frames using filters with Calderón sum equal to one.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality of Gabor, wavelet, and shearlet systems are established, and explicit constructions of pairwise orthogonal Parseval frames are given.
conclusion: The results generalize previous constructions by relaxing stationary assumptions on subgroups, and have potential applications in sampling theory.

title: A Unified Framework For Reaction Systems Based On Interval Structures
authors: Paolo Bottoni, Anna Labella, Ion Petre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reaction systems have evolved into a rich family of computational models differing in their treatment of multiplicities, resource management, concurrency, and state evolution. We introduce a unified semantic framework based on interval structures and interval-based transformation systems. The framework decomposes operational semantics into independent resource, production, update, and execution strategies, providing a common basis for describing, comparing, and constructing reaction-system variants. We show that classical reaction systems, restricted reaction systems, multiset reaction systems, reaction systems with concentration, and resource-preserving multiset reaction systems are all recovered as instantiations of the framework. Quantitative reaction systems are accommodated through an additional preprocessing stage. We further demonstrate that the framework naturally extends beyond reaction systems to other computational models, including Petri nets. The proposed framework provides a common semantic foundation for existing models and a flexible basis for developing and analysing new computational formalisms.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified semantic framework for reaction systems based on interval structures, enabling comparison and construction of various computational models.
motivation: Reaction systems have diversified into many variants with different semantics, lacking a common foundation for analysis and comparison.
method: The authors introduce interval-based transformation systems that decompose operational semantics into independent strategies for resources, production, update, and execution.
result: Classical reaction systems, restricted reaction systems, multiset reaction systems, and others are recovered as instantiations; the framework also extends to Petri nets.
conclusion: The framework provides a flexible basis for developing and analyzing new computational formalisms beyond reaction systems.

title: Graph-Series Semantics And Abel Regularization For Recursive Hybrid Quantum Programs
authors: Jean-Pierre Magnot
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a graded graph-series semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs interpreted in the quantum orchestra monad. Finite terminating executions are represented by directed paths whose edges carry normal completely positive subunital maps and whose terminal vertices carry classical results. Path concatenation defines a graded execution category, while continuation grafting models outcome-dependent sequential composition. We construct a semantic evaluation from admissible execution-graph series to quantum orchestras and prove that it is compatible with both channel composition and Kleisli composition. For finitary recursive programs, the truncation of the execution series at degree [MATH] is shown to coincide with the [MATH]-th Kleene approximant of the associated Scott-continuous recursion functional. Consequently, evaluation of the complete graph series recovers the ordinary least-fixed-point denotation. Weighting a graph of degree [MATH] by [MATH], with [MATH], yields an Abel-regularised semantics whose Scott limit as [MATH] is the unregularised recursive denotation. Equivalently, the parametrisation [MATH] exponentially suppresses long executions and reconstructs the denotation as [MATH]. In a supplementary linear feedback sector, repeated recursion is represented by the execution resolvent [MATH]. We identify [MATH] with an algebraic cross-ratio of graph subspaces. Under Hilbert--Schmidt assumptions, the associated return operator is trace class and defines the Fredholm feedback determinant \( _{F}(I-qST), \) whose zeros detect singular feedback configurations and whose logarithmic expansion records closed loop traversals.
tldr: This paper introduces a graph-series semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs using Abel regularization, but it is highly abstract and mathematical with no clear connection to the user's research directions.
motivation: To provide a rigorous denotational semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs that can handle infinite executions via regularization.
method: The paper defines graded graph-series semantics in the quantum orchestra monad, uses path concatenation and continuation grafting, and applies Abel regularization to sum divergent series.
result: The truncation of execution series at degree n coincides with the n-th Kleene approximant, and the Abel-regularized semantics recovers the unregularized denotation in the limit.
conclusion: The framework provides a consistent semantics for recursive hybrid quantum programs, but its practical relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics is unclear.

title: ReBound: Reuse-Aware Privacy For Interactive Decision Support
authors: Nada Lahjouji, Shufan Zhang, Xi He, Sharad Mehrotra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentially private decision support frameworks answer complex aggregate threshold queries with formal bounds on false negative and false positive rates, but treat each query independently with no memory of past results. In practice, analysts work interactively, issuing sequences of related queries that refine bounds, adjust thresholds, or derive new functions from previous ones. We propose ReBound, a framework that reuses cached results from previous queries to answer new queries at reduced or zero additional privacy cost while maintaining formal utility guarantees. ReBound introduces a reuse framework for multiple refinement types, a cache graph structure for efficient lookup of reusable results, and a negotiation mechanism for when requested bounds cannot be met within budget.
tldr: ReBound is a framework for reusing cached differentially private query results to reduce privacy cost in interactive decision support.
motivation: Existing differential privacy frameworks treat queries independently, ignoring that analysts often issue related queries interactively, leading to unnecessary privacy cost.
method: ReBound introduces a reuse framework for multiple refinement types, a cache graph for efficient lookup, and a negotiation mechanism for unmet bounds.
result: The framework enables answering new queries at reduced or zero additional privacy cost while maintaining formal utility guarantees.
conclusion: ReBound improves privacy efficiency in interactive settings by reusing past query results, but is focused on classical differential privacy, not quantum information.

title: Evaluating Encoding Strategies For Closed-Loop Classification In Biological Neural Networks
authors: Martin Schottlender, Veronika Volkova, Pengjie Zhou, Ruifeng Zheng, Frank H. P. Fitzek, Pit Hofmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacing with Biological Neural Networks (BNNs) requires encoding information into stimulation patterns that can be effectively processed and that enable the underlying system to adapt. Nevertheless, the role of stimulation encoding remains poorly understood. In this work, we compare multiple encoding strategies, including rate-based, phase-based, burst-based, and time-to-first-spike temporal encodings, in a closed-loop neural classification task using cultured BNNs. We encode visual inputs as spatiotemporal stimulation patterns delivered via a Multi-Electrode Array (MEA) and evaluate classification performance for each encoding scheme. We find that burst-based temporal encoding yields the highest observed performance, achieving up to 95.6 % accuracy in a binary classification task, compared to substantially lower performance from rate- and phase-based approaches. We further show that performance is highly sensitive to the spatial distribution of stimulation, with suboptimal electrode selection significantly degrading accuracy. These findings indicate that effective interfacing with biological neural systems requires the joint optimization of temporal and spatial encoding strategies, and highlight temporal encoding as a key design dimension for bio-digital computing.
tldr: This paper evaluates encoding strategies for closed-loop classification in biological neural networks, focusing on temporal and spatial stimulation patterns.
motivation: Effective interfacing with biological neural networks requires understanding how to encode information into stimulation patterns that the network can process and adapt to.
method: The authors compare rate-based, phase-based, burst-based, and time-to-first-spike temporal encodings in a closed-loop classification task using cultured BNNs on a multi-electrode array.
result: Burst-based temporal encoding achieves up to 95.6% accuracy in binary classification, outperforming rate- and phase-based approaches; performance is highly sensitive to spatial electrode selection.
conclusion: Effective bio-digital computing requires joint optimization of temporal and spatial encoding strategies, with temporal encoding being a key design dimension.

title: PriEval-Protect: A Unified Framework For Privacy Evaluation And Protection In Healthcare Systems
authors: Ilef Chebil, Asma El Hadj, Souheib Yousfi, Aroua Hedhili, Layth Sliman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safeguarding patient privacy while enabling meaningful healthcare data use remains critical under GDPR and HIPAA. Existing compliance methods are manual, error-prone, and separate policy audits from data-level assessments. This paper presents PriEval-Protect, a two-phase framework for unified privacy risk evaluation and mitigation. The evaluation phase combines regulatory compliance scoring using a fine-tuned legal LLM with RAG, and technical analysis via encryption type, data architecture, and metrics including similarity, uncertainty, adversary success, and information gain/loss. A composite risk score uses weighted aggregation via Analytic Hierarchy Process. The protection phase recommends countermeasures including federated learning and differential privacy based on assessed risk. Results on hospital documents and datasets demonstrate regulation-aligned, explainable assessments, bridging legal conformance and data-level risk analysis.
tldr: A framework for privacy evaluation and protection in healthcare systems using LLMs and risk metrics.
motivation: Existing compliance methods are manual and separate policy audits from data-level assessments, motivating a unified framework.
method: Combines regulatory compliance scoring via fine-tuned legal LLM with RAG and technical analysis using encryption type, data architecture, and metrics like similarity and adversary success, aggregated via AHP.
result: Demonstrates regulation-aligned, explainable assessments on hospital documents and datasets.
conclusion: The framework bridges legal conformance and data-level risk analysis for healthcare privacy.

title: Half Dualization And Non-invertible Particle-vortex Duality Defect On Lattice
authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce half dualization as a general principle to construct non-invertible duality defects. The construction performs a duality transformation only in a subregion of spacetime, leaving an interface between the original theory and its dual. A non-invertible duality defect can be hosted on this interface. Half dualization is applicable whenever a local duality transformation is available, and does not depend on the spacetime dimension. We demonstrate the construction procedure in the (2+1)-dimensional Villainized charge-[MATH] XY model on a cubic lattice. Half dualization yields a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect whose fusion with its orientation reverse produces a (1+1)-dimensional [MATH] gauge theory on the fusion surface. We then apply half dualization to the [MATH]-gauged XY model relevant to the 3D XY[MATH] transition. In the gauged model, the half dualization interface hosts a gauge covariant duality wall, rather than a genuine gauge invariant duality defect. It flows to an invertible duality defect in infrared when the [MATH] gauge theory is confined or Higgsed.
tldr: This paper introduces half dualization to construct non-invertible particle-vortex duality defects in lattice models, focusing on the (2+1)-dimensional XY model.
motivation: To develop a general principle for constructing non-invertible duality defects that can be applied to various theories and dimensions.
method: Half dualization is performed on a subregion of spacetime, creating an interface between the original theory and its dual, which hosts the duality defect. The construction is demonstrated on the Villainized XY model on a cubic lattice.
result: The half dualization yields a non-invertible particle-vortex duality defect whose fusion with its orientation reverse produces a (1+1)-dimensional gauge theory on the fusion surface. In the gauged XY model, the interface hosts a gauge covariant duality wall that flows to an invertible duality defect in the infrared.
conclusion: Half dualization provides a systematic way to construct non-invertible duality defects, with potential applications in studying dualities and phase transitions in lattice field theories.

title: Reconstruct The Ambient Noise Source From The Multi-frequency Sparse Correlation Data
authors: Hao Gu, Hongxia Guo, Xiang Xu, Yue Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel multi-frequency factorization method to reconstruct the spatial support of the ambient noise source. The proposed method only requires sparse correlation data and has low computational cost. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper develops a multi-frequency factorization method to reconstruct the spatial support of ambient noise sources from sparse correlation data.
motivation: Reconstructing ambient noise sources is important for applications like seismic imaging and ocean acoustics, but existing methods require dense data or high computational cost.
method: The authors propose a novel multi-frequency factorization method that uses sparse correlation data and has low computational cost, with numerical experiments in 2D and 3D.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in reconstructing the spatial support of ambient noise sources.
conclusion: The method provides an efficient way to reconstruct noise sources from sparse data, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Impacts Of Social And Impact Heterogeneity On Social-climate Outcomes
authors: Amrita Punnavajhala, Brian Beckage, Madhur Anand, Daniele Visioni, Jared Farley, Chris T. Bauch
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regional heterogeneity in social characteristics, temperature change, and vulnerability to climate impacts is likely to influence the magnitude of anthropogenic climate change, but has not been considered in coupled social-climate models, which seek to represent interactions between social and climate dynamics. Here, we examine how the projected mean global temperature anomaly and population support for mitigation respond to heterogeneity in these factors across five regions of the world, using a coupled social-climate model. We find that heterogeneity in climate impacts increases the temperature anomaly by 0.2[MATH]C, while social heterogeneity increases it by an additional 0.1[MATH]C. The projected temperature anomaly also increases with higher variability in climate impacts across regions, even for the same average global climate impact. Finally, we identify a social-climate tipping point, where low vulnerability to impacts under existing social conditions in one region can tip the system into an alternative slow-mitigation, high-temperature state. Our results show that heterogeneity in climate impacts leads to higher global mean temperatures and efforts to reduce global disparities could improve both social and climate outcomes.
tldr: This paper studies how regional heterogeneity in social characteristics and climate impacts affects global temperature and mitigation support using a coupled social-climate model.
motivation: Regional heterogeneity in social factors and climate impacts is likely to influence climate change outcomes but has not been considered in coupled social-climate models.
method: The authors develop a coupled social-climate model with five world regions and simulate the effects of heterogeneity in social characteristics, temperature change, and vulnerability to climate impacts.
result: Heterogeneity in climate impacts increases the temperature anomaly by 0.2°C, social heterogeneity adds another 0.1°C, and a social-climate tipping point is identified where low vulnerability in one region leads to a high-temperature state.
conclusion: Reducing global disparities could improve both social and climate outcomes, as heterogeneity leads to higher global mean temperatures.

title: Overlapping Window Tests For Correlation And Trend
authors: Abbas Alhakim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a general framework for constructing and analyzing overlapping sliding-window statistics for dependence and trend detection. For a fixed window size, the overlapping blocks form a Markov chain, and the asymptotic variance of any centered window statistic is determined by the covariance operator of this chain. Using its spectral structure, we obtain an orthogonal decomposition of the space of window functions into components associated with different overlap levels. This leads to a natural notion of incremental dependence information: the part of a statistic that captures exactly the new information introduced by enlarging the window. We give an explicit procedure for extracting these components and apply the method to two classes of examples. For correlation detection, we study symmetric polynomial window functions and identify their informative projected part. For trend detection, we analyze localized rank-based statistics and isolate the contribution of the largest newly introduced lag. The examples also show that different statistics may exhibit different local detection scales, including nonclassical ones. The same viewpoint leads to a natural quantitative measure of incremental information, which can be used to assess how much new dependence structure is captured as the window size increases, and to guide scale selection. Overall, the paper provides a systematic method for designing overlapping-window tests and deriving their asymptotic normalization and local behavior.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for overlapping sliding-window statistics for dependence and trend detection, with applications to correlation and trend detection.
motivation: To provide a systematic method for designing overlapping-window tests and understanding the incremental dependence information as window size increases.
method: The authors model overlapping blocks as a Markov chain, use spectral decomposition to orthogonalize window functions, and extract components capturing new information at each overlap level.
result: They obtain an orthogonal decomposition of window functions, identify informative components for symmetric polynomial and rank-based statistics, and propose a quantitative measure of incremental information.
conclusion: The framework offers a principled way to design and normalize overlapping-window tests, with potential for scale selection in dependence detection.

title: A Generative Model-Free Form Deformation Approach For The Generation Of Mesh Motions With Applications To Pde
authors: Gugliemo Padula, Artem Sinitsa, Gianluigi Rozza
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a topology-agnostic framework for matching deformations of three-dimensional shapes with non-isomorphic mesh graphs by modelling the deformation as the flow of an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE). The velocity field is parameterised by a time-dependent Free Form Deformation (FFD), expressed through displacements of a coarse control lattice, yielding a smooth and low-dimensional representation that decouples the deformation model from the discretisation of the source and target surfaces. Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the induced ODE map is a universal approximator (in the sup norm) for mappings between genus-0 surfaces, providing a theoretical expressivity guarantee. To further compress the representation and enable probabilistic inference, we couple the ODE--FFD model with a flow-based generative approach in the TarFlow framework, learning a compact latent parametrisation over time series of FFD maps. The resulting method supports efficient sampling and optimisation of plausible deformation trajectories while preserving mesh quality, and it enables scalable reduced-order modelling. Experiments on deforming-body flow benchmarks demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency of reduced-order models constructed from the learned latent dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a generative model-free form deformation approach for mesh motions with applications to PDEs.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a topology-agnostic framework for matching deformations of 3D shapes with non-isomorphic mesh graphs, enabling efficient reduced-order modeling for deforming-body flow problems.
method: They model deformation as an ODE flow, parameterize the velocity field using time-dependent Free Form Deformation (FFD), and couple it with a flow-based generative model (TarFlow) to learn a compact latent parametrization.
result: The method provides a universal approximation guarantee for genus-0 surface mappings and demonstrates improved accuracy and computational efficiency in reduced-order models on deforming-body flow benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a scalable and efficient approach for generating mesh motions and reduced-order models, with potential applications in computational fluid dynamics and shape analysis.

title: A Unified Approach For Testing In Hilbert Spaces On Incomplete Data
authors: Philipp W\"ubbolding Daniel Gaigall
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider statistical testing on the basis of incomplete observations with values in a separable Hilbert space, where the dimension is possibly large or even infinite. The general Hilbert space setting allows various data types as they arise in modern applications, in particular high dimensional and functional data. Possible Hilbert space testing problems are goodness-of-fit, symmetry, homogeneity and independence. We present an approach for modeling incomplete data that covers several problems in practice, e.g., ultra high dimensional random vectors with missing entries or partially observed stochastic processes. We identify a specific structure (independent and identically distributed) in the incomplete data that enables the analysis of statistical procedures with the help of suitable mathematical results (e.g., laws of large numbers and central limit theorems). Additionally, a general and novel concept for testing different hypotheses in this situation is suggested and sketched for the example of testing goodness-of-fit for normality.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified statistical testing framework for incomplete data in Hilbert spaces, covering high-dimensional and functional data.
motivation: Incomplete data (e.g., missing entries, partially observed processes) is common in modern applications, but existing testing methods are often ad-hoc or limited to specific settings.
method: The authors model incomplete data as independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) observations in a separable Hilbert space, and develop a general concept for testing hypotheses such as goodness-of-fit, symmetry, homogeneity, and independence.
result: The approach leverages laws of large numbers and central limit theorems in Hilbert spaces to enable analysis of statistical procedures, and is illustrated for testing normality.
conclusion: The paper provides a unified theoretical framework for hypothesis testing with incomplete functional or high-dimensional data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Almost Disjoint Families And Johnson-Lindenstrauss Spaces
authors: Antonio Avil\'es, Grzegorz Plebanek, Luis S\'aenz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every almost disjoint family [MATH] of infinite subsets of [MATH] gives rise to a scattered compact space [MATH] and a family of Johnson-Lindenstrauss spaces JL[MATH]. We consider almost disjoint families arising from finitely branching trees and investigate whether they define homeomorphic compacta and isomorphic Banach spaces.
tldr: This paper studies almost disjoint families of subsets of natural numbers and their associated Johnson-Lindenstrauss Banach spaces, focusing on topological and isomorphic properties.
motivation: To understand the structure of scattered compact spaces and Banach spaces arising from almost disjoint families defined by finitely branching trees.
method: The authors consider almost disjoint families constructed from finitely branching trees and analyze the homeomorphism type of the associated compact spaces and isomorphism type of the Banach spaces.
result: They investigate conditions under which different trees yield homeomorphic compacta or isomorphic Banach spaces.
conclusion: The work contributes to set-theoretic topology and Banach space theory, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Model Predictive Control For Laser Thermal Processing: Operator Learning, Closed-loop Validation, And Out-of-distribution Analysis
authors: Smajil Halilovic, Yuchen Zhang, Daniel M. Tartakovsky
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laser-based thermal processing, such as laser powder bed fusion, requires tight regulation of the peak surface temperature: heat accumulates where the moving source re-enters previously heated material, driving the temperature out of its process window and causing defects. High-fidelity thermal models capture this physics but are too slow for online optimization, which motivates fast, differentiable, and generalizable surrogates. We develop and validate a complete surrogate-based control pipeline that regulates the maximum surface temperature of a moving laser on a 304-stainless-steel substrate. We also determine conditions under which our surrogate can be trusted inside the control loop by probing its out-of-distribution limits. A key component of our surrogate is a multi-step deep operator network bespoke for moving sources: its branch subnetwork encodes the future power and trajectory (position and velocity) sequence, while its trunk encodes the current peak temperature and the temperature at the future laser locations, yielding a one-shot five-step prediction. By way of illustration, we use this surrogate as a smooth (algebraic-rectifier) nonlinear program inside a receding-horizon model predictive controller solved in CasADi/IPOPT. The surrogate forward pass is over thousand times faster than the equivalent finite-difference steps. We show that aggregate open-loop accuracy is necessary but not sufficient for control-readiness: two surrogates with near-identical offline error behave drastically differently in closed loop. A controlled two-ensemble data design reduces a 91 K path-corner underprediction failure to 1.4 K, and a calibrated one-sided constraint margin of 13 K yields zero violations of the true upper bound on all tested paths.
tldr: This paper develops a surrogate-based model predictive control pipeline for laser thermal processing, focusing on operator learning and closed-loop validation.
motivation: Laser-based thermal processing requires tight temperature regulation to avoid defects, but high-fidelity models are too slow for online optimization.
method: A multi-step deep operator network is used as a surrogate to predict temperature, integrated into a receding-horizon model predictive controller solved with CasADi/IPOPT.
result: The surrogate is over 1000 times faster than finite-difference steps; a two-ensemble data design reduces prediction failure from 91 K to 1.4 K, and a calibrated margin yields zero violations.
conclusion: Aggregate open-loop accuracy is necessary but not sufficient for control-readiness; the surrogate-based control pipeline is effective for laser thermal processing.

title: Hybrid Gkb Methods For X-Ray Tomography Problems With Unmatched Back Projector
authors: Rosemary Renaut Abdulmajeed Alsubhi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: X ray Computed Tomography (CT) is a widely used imaging modality in medical, industrial, and scientific applications. In practical CT implementations, forward, A, and back projection, B, operators are often constructed using different discretization schemes to improve computational efficiency on available software and hardware platforms. Consequently, the resulting projector pair is generally unmatched, meaning that the back projector is not the exact adjoint of the forward projector. This mismatch alters the mathematical properties of the reconstruction problem and can affect the convergence behavior of iterative reconstruction methods. Previous studies have proposed AB and BA Golub Kahan bidiagonalization (GKB) methods, as well as GMRES and hybrid GMRES methods, for solving CT reconstruction problems with unmatched projector pairs, demonstrating reduced semiconvergence effects compared with conventional approaches. In this work, we develop hybrid variants of the AB- and BA-GKB algorithms by incorporating regularization within the projection process. The singular value decomposition for the operator on the projected space is used to efficiently reconstruct the solution, and to automatically select the regularization parameter using either the L-curve or generalized cross-validation. Numerical experiments on several CT reconstruction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid methods in improving robustness against semiconvergence.
tldr: This paper develops hybrid GKB methods for CT reconstruction with unmatched forward/back projector pairs, focusing on computational efficiency and regularization.
motivation: In practical CT, forward and back projectors are often mismatched due to different discretization schemes, which degrades convergence of iterative methods. Existing GKB methods reduce semiconvergence but lack regularization.
method: Hybrid variants of AB- and BA-GKB algorithms are proposed, incorporating regularization via SVD on the projected space and automatic parameter selection using L-curve or GCV.
result: Numerical experiments on CT reconstruction problems show improved robustness against semiconvergence compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: The hybrid GKB methods effectively handle unmatched projector pairs and enhance reconstruction quality in CT imaging.

title: Residual-Christoffel Sampling For Random Feature Collocation Of Linear PDEs
authors: Yangshuai Wang Jiale Linghu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random feature collocation fixes a randomly generated trial space and determines its coefficients from a linear least-squares system. Stability then depends on whether the sampled residual equations represent the geometry induced by the differential operator. We construct an operator-aware discretization in which the operator-applied features determine both the collocation measure and a coefficient whitening map. The randomized scheme combines a residual-Christoffel density with inverse-density weights, while a deterministic scalar-row alternative maximizes successive regularized log-determinant increments. Conditional on the realized trial space, the sampled whitened interior Gram is a spectral approximation to the reference Gram on the retained residual space, with sample complexity linear in the retained dimension up to a logarithmic factor. For uniformly analytic residual kernels, the associated operator has stretched-exponentially decaying eigenvalues and ridge effective dimension that is polylogarithmic in the inverse ridge scale. Experiments on scalar and vector equations, varied geometries, and one to three spatial dimensions show that residual-space sampling and whitening produce numerically full-rank transformed systems with substantially smaller condition numbers and iteration counts. The deterministic construction attains the lowest errors at the smallest scalar sample sizes. Residual-space geometry therefore yields a principled design for stable strong-form random feature collocation.
tldr: This paper proposes a residual-Christoffel sampling method for random feature collocation of linear PDEs, focusing on numerical stability and efficiency.
motivation: Random feature collocation methods suffer from ill-conditioned systems; the authors aim to design an operator-aware discretization that improves stability and sample complexity.
method: They construct a residual-Christoffel density combined with inverse-density weights and a deterministic scalar-row alternative that maximizes regularized log-determinant increments, then analyze the spectral approximation properties of the whitened Gram matrix.
result: The method achieves numerically full-rank transformed systems with lower condition numbers and iteration counts; sample complexity is linear in retained dimension up to a logarithmic factor.
conclusion: Residual-space geometry provides a principled design for stable strong-form random feature collocation, demonstrated on various PDEs.

title: Computing Strong Rank-Revealing Factorizations For Matrices With Orthonormal Rows
authors: Anil Damle
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a pivoting strategy due to Stewart (based on work by Bischof) computes a strong rank-revealing factorization when applied to a matrix with orthonormal rows. When paired with the classical column selection algorithm of Golub, Klema, and Stewart (GKS) it helps achieve rank-[MATH] approximation accuracy bounds and basis conditioning as good as those from applying a strong rank-revealing factorization directly to A. We then extend this framework in two directions: (1) providing analysis of GKS when only approximations of right singular vectors are available and (2) providing a randomized variant of the pivoting strategy for matrices with orthonormal rows that achieves the same theoretical guarantees but can return the desired subset two orders of magnitude faster than the deterministic variant.
tldr: This paper presents algorithms for computing strong rank-revealing factorizations of matrices with orthonormal rows, with applications in numerical linear algebra.
motivation: Strong rank-revealing factorizations are important for low-rank approximations and subset selection, but existing algorithms may not be efficient for matrices with orthonormal rows.
method: The paper analyzes Stewart's pivoting strategy for matrices with orthonormal rows, extends the GKS algorithm to handle approximate singular vectors, and introduces a randomized variant for faster computation.
result: The proposed methods achieve approximation accuracy and basis conditioning comparable to direct strong rank-revealing factorizations, with the randomized variant being up to two orders of magnitude faster.
conclusion: The algorithms provide efficient and accurate tools for rank-revealing factorizations in numerical linear algebra, but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Spectrally Damped Tensor Randomized Kaczmarz Method For Doubly Noisy Tensor Systems
authors: Jiyoung Choi Nahyun Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor randomized Kaczmarz (TRK) methods are efficient row-action solvers for tensor linear systems under the t-product framework. We study their behavior under a doubly noisy perturbation model. In this model, both the system tensor and the right-hand side tensor are corrupted. We first analyze standard TRK and derive an expected error recursion with two terms. One term is contractive, and the other is a persistent perturbation term. This explains the noise-limited and semi-convergent behavior that can occur when the observed tensor system is inconsistent. We then introduce a spectrally damped tensor randomized Kaczmarz method (SD-TRK). We prove an expected error recursion for SD-TRK that separates error propagation from noise injection. The bound makes explicit a speed-robustness trade-off. We also give an FFT-based implementation that applies the damped update slice-wise in the Fourier domain. This implementation allows frequency-dependent damping parameters in practice. Numerical experiments on synthetic tensor systems illustrate the stabilization behavior of SD-TRK relative to standard TRK in noisy and ill-conditioned settings. We also include a two-pass image reconstruction comparison under the same noisy reconstruction pipeline.
tldr: This paper proposes a spectrally damped tensor randomized Kaczmarz method for solving tensor linear systems with noise in both the system tensor and right-hand side.
motivation: Standard tensor randomized Kaczmarz methods exhibit noise-limited and semi-convergent behavior when the observed tensor system is inconsistent due to double-sided noise.
method: The authors introduce a spectrally damped variant (SD-TRK) that uses frequency-dependent damping parameters in the Fourier domain via an FFT-based implementation, and derive expected error recursions.
result: The SD-TRK method separates error propagation from noise injection, providing a speed-robustness trade-off, and numerical experiments show stabilization in noisy and ill-conditioned settings.
conclusion: The proposed method improves robustness to noise in tensor linear systems, with potential applications in image reconstruction.

title: Spectral-Informed Neural Networks Outperform Spectral Methods In High-dimensional PDEs
authors: Ivan Oseledets Tianchi Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For low-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods can achieve exceptionally high accuracy. For middle-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods remain feasible through specific techniques such as sparse grids or hyperbolic cross. However, for high-dimensional problems ([MATH]), spectral methods suffer frome the curse of dimensionality. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising approach to overcome this challenge, offering scalability to high dimensions, but often suffer from limited accuracy and efficiency. Recently proposed spectral-informed neural networks (SINNs) combine spectral methods with PINNs, operating directly in the spectral domain to avoid spatial derivative computations and to reduce memory consumption. In this work, we introduce Modified SINNs, which integrate coefficient decay scaling and basis embeddings motivated by harmonic analysis to enhance accuracy in high-dimensional problems and enable accurate approximation of unknown spectral coefficients. Numerical experiments on steady and time-dependent partial differential equations demonstrate that Modified SINNs outperform sparse grid spectral methods on middle-dimensional problems with incomplete spectral information and achieve superior accuracy compared to PINNs on high-dimensional problems.
tldr: This paper proposes Modified Spectral-Informed Neural Networks (SINNs) for solving high-dimensional PDEs, combining spectral methods with physics-informed neural networks.
motivation: Spectral methods suffer from the curse of dimensionality in high-dimensional problems, while PINNs offer scalability but limited accuracy. The authors aim to combine the strengths of both approaches.
method: Modified SINNs integrate coefficient decay scaling and basis embeddings motivated by harmonic analysis, operating directly in the spectral domain to avoid spatial derivative computations.
result: Numerical experiments show that Modified SINNs outperform sparse grid spectral methods on middle-dimensional problems with incomplete spectral information and achieve superior accuracy compared to PINNs on high-dimensional problems.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively enhances accuracy and efficiency for high-dimensional PDEs, demonstrating the potential of spectral-informed neural networks.

title: Approximation Of Solutions Of Parameter-dependent Problems By Residual Neural Networks
authors: Ana Carpio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a convergent scheme to train neural networks involving analytic activation functions based on gradient flows. Convergence properties are guaranteed by Lojasiewicz theory. The main advantage of this approach is its simplicity of implementation. The coefficients of the network are approximated by solving a system of ordinary differential equations. We test the method by constructing residual neural network approximations of solutions of parametric problems. The dependence of the solutions of simple ordinary differential equations on a few parameters is correctly reproduced. The solutions of inverse problems involving wave constraints which depend on a few parameters can be reasonably approximated, even in regions in which the problem is severely ill posed.
tldr: This paper develops a convergent training scheme for residual neural networks to approximate solutions of parameter-dependent problems, using gradient flows and Lojasiewicz theory.
motivation: To provide a simple and theoretically grounded method for training neural networks to solve parametric problems, including inverse problems with wave constraints.
method: The network coefficients are approximated by solving a system of ordinary differential equations derived from gradient flows, with convergence guaranteed by Lojasiewicz theory.
result: The method correctly reproduces solutions of simple ODEs depending on a few parameters and reasonably approximates solutions of inverse problems with wave constraints, even in severely ill-posed regions.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a simple implementation with guaranteed convergence, suitable for parametric problems and inverse problems.

title: The Value Of Perfect Endpoint Forecasts For Offshore-Wind Thermal Firming
authors: Arash Khojaste, Geoffrey Pritchard, Golbon Zakeri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecast value depends not only on accuracy but also on the information structure available to the operating model. We study a diagnostic current-endpoint-only forecast for offshore-wind thermal firming: at hour t, the controller observes the current net-demand state z_t and one perfect future target z_{t+h}, but not the intermediate path or earlier endpoint messages. Unlike rolling path forecasts, these endpoint information sets are not nested in h. We embed the signal in a cyclostationary MDP using quantile Fourier regression states estimated from ISO New England load and offshore wind data, and solve annual state-action-frequency LPs for h = 1, . . . , 6. A one-hour endpoint forecast reduces annual firming cost by 8.07%, while a six-hour endpoint reduces it by 2.28%. The decreasing profile shows that a single farther endpoint is less actionable for a one-step ramping decision, without implying that longer rolling forecasts are less valuable.
tldr: This paper studies the value of perfect endpoint forecasts for offshore-wind thermal firming using a cyclostationary MDP.
motivation: To understand how forecast information structure affects operational cost reduction in renewable energy integration.
method: Embed a current-endpoint-only forecast in a cyclostationary MDP with quantile Fourier regression states, solving annual state-action-frequency LPs for different forecast horizons.
result: A one-hour endpoint forecast reduces annual firming cost by 8.07%, while a six-hour endpoint reduces it by 2.28%.
conclusion: A single farther endpoint is less actionable for one-step ramping decisions, but this does not imply longer rolling forecasts are less valuable.

title: Operational Evidence Gaps For LLMs In Fraud Detection And Trust-and-Safety Workflows
authors: Keyur Gabani
abstract: ArXiv:2607.13078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are now proposed for fraud detection, scam investigation, content moderation, and other trust-and-safety workflows. Much of the public literature still evaluates them as models, with less attention to their behavior as components in operational pipelines. This creates a practical evidence question: what would justify placing an LLM inside a live workflow with latency, cost, escalation, human-review, and adversarial-risk constraints? We address this question through a fraud-first survey of deployment evidence.
